finding.clause: §5.3 NR-12(b) (with PS-5's operational definition and NR-1's last sentence); also NR-12(d)
finding.quote: If any premise is a PS-5 structure (an invariant, Gibbs or KMS measure; …), whether supplied, hidden or generated by 𝒦, then every claim whose derivation passes through it is STANDARD-IMPLIED and earns 0.
finding.problem:
PS-5 is defined operationally: any structure from which a standard theorem derives a fluctuation–response identity. A standard theorem (the NESS FDR of Agarwal and Seifert–Speck) derives one from the stationary law of any Markov generator. Round-3 M7 established this and moved generated PS-5 from NR-1 into NR-12(b), which now poisons it.

Every stationary card's ℛ★ concerns response about the reference state of its own dynamics (a₀ and P_{a₀}; RH-STAT holds by the hostile default). Its derivation therefore 'passes through' a generated invariant measure. Under CV-1 every such ℛ★ is STANDARD-IMPLIED and earns 0, so b_J = 0 and the card is NON-COMPRESSIVE. A deterministic card with an invariant reference measure is caught too.

NR-12(d) adds a second literal kill. 'On an instance whose reference state is not KMS, if ℛ★'s credited content vanishes there' fires on any single such instance, for example a weakly coupled draw.

CHARTER TEST pattern: a card proves a non-standard joint relation from its generator, uses the generator's stationary law only as the chart's reference state, and invokes no FDR or fluctuation theorem. Terminal: STANDARD-IMPLIED.
finding.fix_wording:
Append to NR-12(b): "A generated invariant (stationary) law that is not itself KMS/Gibbs, detailed-balanced, microreversible or of exponential-family form is such a premise only where the derivation applies to it a standard theorem that takes it as a hypothesis (an STD-3 NESS form, regression, a fluctuation theorem, an Onsager form). Its use as the reference state, or as an intermediate object to which no such theorem is applied, does not make the claim STANDARD-IMPLIED. Q3, NR-12(c) and §13.4 apply unchanged."

In NR-12(d), replace the first clause with: "If ℛ★'s credited content is present on KMS instances and vanishes on the instances whose reference state is certified non-KMS, …"

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute the defect and could not. Read as a whole, the charter makes an honest stationary non-KMS card fail.

1. The text is explicit, so there is nothing to read charitably. NR-12(b)'s own parenthetical lists "an invariant … measure" as a PS-5 premise. It applies "whether supplied, hidden or generated by 𝒦". Generated premises are intermediate results by definition, so a derived stationary law counts. Three clauses route generated PS-5 straight to NR-12(b): NR-1's last sentences, §13.6 ("Its consequences follow NR-12(b)") and the round-3 M7 note ("generated PS-5 still makes every claim through it STANDARD-IMPLIED"). M7 itself says that the NESS FDR (Agarwal; Seifert–Speck) is derivable from any Markov generator's stationary law. A stationary path law is shift-invariant, so it is itself an invariant measure. CV-1 resolves any remaining doubt about "passes through" against the card.

2. No other clause rescues the card.
   - §1.5 requires a lock fiber regime-matched to the platform: H(fiber) ⊇ H_host(platform). On a stationary NESS platform RH-STAT holds, so the lock fiber must be stationary too. The card cannot escape by using a non-stationary reference.
   - If 𝒦 states stationarity itself, NR-1 flags it ("invariant or reference measure"). It is then SUPPLIED, and §5.6 makes it CARD-RELOCATED if ℛ★ uses it.
   - The only escape left is to prove ℛ★ for every initial law. That fails for response relations about a reference state.
   - So every card on a stationary platform where RH-KMS fails earns b_J = 0 and is NON-COMPRESSIVE. That is exactly the platform class G2-12 item 4 tells authors to target.
   - The literal reading also empties clauses that assume such cards can earn credit:
     - STD-3 and Q3(f): "response = X·correlation" is allowed "unless X is predicted from interface-side data and beats B-SRB";
     - §13.7: credit in regimes where FDT is silent;
     - NR-12(d)'s own premise of non-KMS reference states;
     - R2-A m8's purpose: do not kill every stochastic rule.
   - FDT content is already removed by §13.1, STD-3 (NESS forms), Q3(e) and B-SRB. The blanket poison goes beyond what is needed.
   - A possible second route is IP-6 closure: a used structure matching VB-17 (invariant measure) "is that item", and an undeclared match → RELOCATED. ST-6 rules this reading out. There the FDT derivation uses a generated detailed-balance invariant law and reaches S5, not S3, and CV-7 voids readings that change self-test verdicts. So IP-6 adds no kill of its own.

3. NR-12(d) is a real secondary hidden kill. Its "On an instance … if credited content vanishes there" is existential. It needs no evidence that the content was present on KMS instances, so the inference "it lived in FDT" is unsupported. It also fires on degenerate non-KMS instances, such as near-decoupled draws where every lock observable is within r_lock of its decoupled value. G2-12 item 5 already excluded such points for NR-4 for the same reason.

4. This is in CR-1 scope (an honest card failing). It cannot be loosened after Card 1 under §19.2.
verdict.fix_problems:
1. **The exemption may never apply.** It is keyed to "not itself KMS/Gibbs … or of exponential-family form". Under CV-1, every full-support law on a finite space is Gibbs and exponential-family in −log π, so a hostile auditor can void the exemption every time. The fix should use the operational §13.2 surrogates instead (RH-KMS, RH-DB, RH-GGE), certified under BP-4 to fail by at least δ_RH.

2. **Loophole through NR-17's last sentence.** That sentence sends a generated PS-5 sub-conjunct to NR-12(b) and applies no JN to it. With the exemption, a cheap 𝒦₂ that is L₀-equivalent to the generated non-KMS stationary law, and that alone imposes ℛ★ under NR-17(a) or (b), escapes both rules. NR-12(b) no longer fires and JN is never applied. The fix must say that JN applies to such a law in full.

3. **"Applies to it a standard theorem" is too loose.** An inline re-derivation of the NESS FDR, used as one step inside an otherwise non-standard derivation, may escape the per-step poison. Q3(e) and §13.1 catch only an ℛ★ that is itself 𝒮-implied. The fix should reuse PS-5's own test: the theorem is cited, re-derived, or exhibited by a reviewer as L₀-equivalent within c_dec bits to the step.

4. **"Any theorem taking it as a hypothesis" is too strict.** That reaches Wiener–Khinchin and other stationarity mathematics, so it leaves part of the kill in place. The poison should be limited to what makes the law PS-5 in the first place: fluctuation–response identities, fluctuation theorems, and regression or Onsager forms.

5. **Card-declared parities.** Certifying that RH-KMS fails depends on the parities the card declares (CR-2 Q-7). The exemption becomes a new credit route that rests on them, so the auditor should choose the parities.

6. **The "apply unchanged" list is incomplete.** It omits §13.1 and B-SRB, which is where FDT content is actually removed.

7. **The NR-12(d) rewrite over-loosens.** "Vanishes on the instances whose reference state is certified non-KMS" reads as all such instances. Content present on KMS instances would then escape if it survives on even one non-KMS instance. A better fix keeps the existential test and adds two things: the missing condition that the content was present on a KMS instance, and an exclusion of decoupled points. It should also restrict the test to in-domain instances.
verdict.final_wording:
NR-12(b): append after "A hidden premise → RELOCATED.":
"A stationary (invariant) law that 𝒦 generates, and that is certified under BP-4 (time-reversal parities chosen by the auditor) to fail RH-KMS, RH-DB and RH-GGE by at least δ_RH, is such a premise only for a derivation step that uses a fluctuation–response identity of any order, a fluctuation theorem, a regression relation or an Onsager form that a standard theorem derives from it (e.g. the STD-3 NESS and effective-temperature forms, Harada–Sasa). This holds whether that theorem is cited, re-derived, or exhibited by a reviewer as L₀-equivalent within c_dec bits to the step. Its use as the reference state of 𝒦's own dynamics, or as an intermediate object that no such step uses, does not make a claim STANDARD-IMPLIED. §13.1, Q3, NR-12(c), B-SRB and §13.4 apply unchanged. NR-17's last sentence does not divert such a law; JN applies to it in full."

NR-12(d): replace with:
"(d) If ℛ★'s credited content is present on an in-domain instance whose reference state is KMS (RH-KMS holding under BP-4) and vanishes on an in-domain instance whose reference state is certified non-KMS, it lived in FDT and earns 0. An instance at which every lock observable lies within r_lock of its S–E-decoupled value is not used for this test (as for NR-4, G2-12 item 5)."

finding.clause: §2.2 𝔐_std; §15.4 ranges and witness rules; §2.5 c_ι; BP-7; §15.5 J_SRB; MC-4 live rival
finding.quote: Ranges: β ∈ [0.25, 4]; frequencies ∈ [0.5, 2]; couplings ∈ [0, 1]; N_B ≤ 8 … If no m ∈ 𝔐_std(ι | H) accepts the card's (Π, [h], T_Π), then c_ι := κ_ι := 0
finding.fix_wording: Add to §2.2, cited in §15.4 and §15.5: "A parameter or structure of an HB family that θ_dict(𝒞_ι) or a BP-5 input fixes (including a measured spectral density and the bath modes it requires) takes that value even outside the §15.4 ranges and N_B. The ranges bound only parameters left free. This holds for 𝔐_std(ι | H), FB, FB(u), c_ι, c_f, dim_lb and every Q3, J_SRB and live-rival witness. It places the frozen families at the instance's own inputs and is not an enlargement under BP-7. An empty J_SRB is never scored by the J_K ⊇ J_SRB test."

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute the defect and could not. Read as a whole, the charter makes an honest card fail in both of the ways the report describes.

**Why the defect holds.**
- **The model grammar is capped by the ranges.** §2.2 defines 𝔐_std(ι|H) as the B-HB families, their compositions within the frozen ranges, and card-added models from those families within the same ranges. §15.4 makes those ranges part of the library: β ∈ [0.25,4], ω ∈ [0.5,2], couplings ∈ [0,1], N_B ≤ 8 (Appendix A repeats them). The §15.4 witness rules apply the same cap to every Q3 witness and dim_lb witness.
- **Condition (iii) of §2.2 forces the instance's inputs onto the model.** A member must use the card's inputs through θ_dict. The auditor may narrow θ_dict to the declared FR11 meaning, and CV-2 lets the auditor lower credit.
- **AI-3 draws spread far beyond the ranges.** Continuous primitives are drawn log-uniformly over the default range [10⁻³,10³] (§1.5, App. A). DIF-7 can exclude at most 10% of draws (θ_gen = 0.9).
- **One bad instance zeroes all credit.** On any instance where θ_dict(𝒞_ι) lands outside the ranges, 𝔐_std(ι|H) is empty. The §2.5 clause then sets c_ι = κ_ι = 0. b_J takes its minimum over all of I_𝒦, so b_J = 0, which is NON-COMPRESSIVE (KU-11). With 100 instances spread over six decades, this is close to certain for any card whose continuous inputs carry a physical meaning.

**Possible rescues, and why each fails.**
- *Rescaling units.* The charter does not grant it, and CV-1 resolves the doubt against the card. Even if it were granted, it cannot fit a frequency or coupling spread of several decades into a window of a factor of 4, or βω > 8.
- *Composition.* It removes the N_B limit, since members can be juxtaposed. It does not lift the β, ω or coupling limits.
- *BP-7.* It forbids the evaluator from enlarging FB or dim_lb.
- *Choosing lock fibers in range.* This does not help. BP-3 regime matching is about the hypotheses H, not parameter values, and J_SRB and the live rival use the BP-5 inputs measured on the platform.
- *The lock side has no escape.* If no in-range witness is consistent with the BP-5 inputs, Q3(a) has no witness, there is no live rival, and J_SRB = ∅. Then MC-4 fails ("no two certified witnesses differ", b_meas = −∞), and the §15.5 table returns RESTATED.

Most real P-2 and P-3 platforms fall in this case: broadband spectral densities, βħω > 8, more than 4 quantum sites. A card can avoid the problem only by using discrete inputs alone and a narrowband classical platform. That is a hidden kill of a legitimate class, which is exactly what G2-12 says CR-1 must repair.

**Adjacent issue, outside this report.** For scope G, App. A defines the window W as the observable's range over B-HB at the standard reference parameters. A platform outside the ranges may then fall partly outside W, which would shrink N(J_SRB ∩ W). This deserves a separate check.
verdict.fix_problems:
1. **The fix leaves out the comparison classes and the family cap, and that opens a loophole.**
   - The c_J(b) comparison classes M are "a B-HB family, a composition within the frozen ranges", and M receives the instance inputs through θ_dict.
   - Under the proposed fix, FB becomes nonempty on instances outside the ranges. A range-bound B-HB M still cannot take those inputs, so it cannot realize Im ∩ FB and does not qualify. (b) then stops binding through B-HB, and "If no class qualifies, the family cap imposes no bound."
   - Q3(b) genericity families have the same problem: they are defined as §2.5(b) classes.
   - Result: a card gains by having inputs outside the ranges, because the hostile caps disappear. The rule must apply equally to every B-HB use, including §2.5(b), the family cap c_fam and Q3(b)–(c).

2. **"An empty J_SRB is never scored by the J_K ⊇ J_SRB test" is unnecessary and ambiguous.**
   - Once witnesses are placed at the platform's inputs, J_SRB is not empty.
   - When J_SRB is truly empty, MC-4 already fails (no live rival, "no two certified witnesses differ", and b_meas = −∞, which still gives RESTATED through the second disjunct).
   - The sentence could be misread as sending an empty J_SRB to the "Otherwise → PASS" row. Drop it.

3. **"Structure that θ_dict fixes" places no bound on a fixed value being varied.**
   - The card declares θ_dict, so the wording should say that an out-of-range fixed value is never a free axis and that free parameters stay inside the ranges.
   - That keeps the claim "not an enlargement under BP-7" true. Many modes are already allowed through composition, so nothing new is needed for the mode count beyond the fixed-value rule.

4. **Missing cross-reference (minor).** §15.5 and the §15.4 witness rules should cite the new clause, so that the witness requirement "within the frozen ranges" is read the same way everywhere.
verdict.final_wording:
§2.2, new bullet after the θ_dict bullet:
"- **Fixed values.** Where θ_dict(𝒞_ι), or a BP-5 input measured on the lock platform, fixes a parameter or structure of an HB family (including a measured spectral density and the modes it requires), the family takes that value even outside the §15.4 ranges and N_B. A value so fixed is never varied. The ranges and N_B bound only the parameters left free, and those stay within them. This holds wherever 𝔐_std(ι | H), a B-HB family or composition, or the §15.4 witness rules are used: FB, FB(u), c_ι, c_f, dim_lb, the admissible comparison classes and family cap of §2.5, Q3(a)–(c), J_SRB and the MC-4 live rival. Placing a family at the instance's or platform's own inputs is not an enlargement under BP-7."

§15.4, append to the Ranges bullet:
"The ranges and N_B bound only parameters left free; values fixed by θ_dict(𝒞_ι) or a BP-5 input follow §2.2 (fixed values), for witnesses as for every other use."

§15.5, append to the first bullet:
"Witnesses consistent with every BP-5 input are taken under §2.2 (fixed values)."

(Do not add the proposed sentence on empty J_SRB.)

finding.clause: §3.1 Q1 (with §1.5 AI-4, §15.1 B-SEL embeddings, §15.9 pool (a) SEL-H)
finding.quote: Im(ι) ⊆ Z(ℛ★) on every in-domain instance (AI-1 to AI-4 and the holdouts)
finding.problem:
AI-4 is the battery embeddings via Emb, i.e. the B-SEL scenarios, and 'the holdouts' include the SEL-H support cases. On these instances:
- the protocols are measurement contexts, with no a₀ and none of the frozen ramp templates, so 𝔄 and the chart φ_ι are undefined;
- the records are discrete outcomes, but 'ε is always computed on continuous records', and ε at E₂±/T_caus on such laws 'is undefined and a claim using it fails Q8'.

So Im(ι) in chart coordinates, and ℛ★ itself, are undefined on instances Q1 names as in-domain. Under CV-1 and DC-10 (UNDECIDED = FAIL), Q1 fails, giving CARD-UNFORCED. This hits every card, because G-SEL requires every card to embed Bell scenarios.
finding.fix_wording: Q1: "Im(ι) ⊆ Z(ℛ★) on every in-domain instance on which the frozen chart is defined: AI-1 to AI-3, the lock fibers, every AI-4 embedding whose repertoire is the frozen templates, and the reciprocity and AI-5 holdouts. … B-SEL embeddings and SEL-H items (measurement contexts) are scored by §15.1 only. An undefined or ⊥ chart coordinate on any other in-domain instance is a Q1 failure."

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute the finding by reading the charter as a whole. It survives.

1. AI-4 is in Q1's scope, and AI-4 means the B-SEL embeddings. Q1 (l.666) lists "(AI-1 to AI-4 and the holdouts)" as the in-domain instances. AI-4 is "Battery embeddings via Emb" (l.388). The only battery Emb embeds is the selectivity interface (C15; §15.1 "Embedding"; §5.2 "Ξ→battery" map). Q1's own grade clause asks for "exact computation on every finite battery instance", so Q1 is meant to run on battery embeddings. "The holdouts" covers every §15.9 pool, including pool (a), the SEL-H support-level cases.

2. On these instances the chart is undefined. §1.7 builds the repertoire from the frozen templates and needs a₀, A_{r★} and A_{r★★}. A B-SEL embedding has measurement contexts instead (§15.1: measurements → interventions, contexts → jointly performed protocol sets). So 𝔄 is undefined there. Dom_gate is empty, because the carrier form must hold for every a in A_{r★★}. The scope-G chart (response functionals at the frozen templates and grid) and the scope-Q chart ("on the template grid") have nothing to evaluate. Records come in the scenario's own alphabet, and Appendix A says "ε is always computed on continuous records". So the ε coordinates that §2.5 puts into Im(ι) are not computed. Under §1.4 a claim that uses an undefined ε fails Q8. This hits scope-Q cards hardest, and G2-12 item 4 makes scope Q the expected route.

3. Every candidate rescue fails:
   - **Vacuous truth.** One could argue that with no A ∈ 𝔄, "for every A ∈ 𝔄" holds vacuously. That reading is contestable, and CV-1 resolves contested readings against the card. DC-6 adds that an unscorable mandatory item means the gate is not passed.
   - **Declaring a narrower domain.** A card could try to declare a C16/DIF-7 domain predicate that leaves out Emb(Σ). Q1's parenthetical names AI-4 explicitly, and CV-1 again rules against the card. The predicate would also have to leave out the SEL-H holdouts.
   - **A later owner ruling.** A CV-7 interpretation after the fact is a dispute-by-dispute gamble. G2-12 asks that too-strict defects be fixed before Card 1.

4. Every card is hit. G-SEL makes Bell embeddings mandatory, and S5 (Q1 → CARD-UNFORCED) runs before S8. So this is a hidden kill: too strict, not a loophole, and inside CR-1's scope. One small correction to the report: the clauses that actually do the work are CV-1, DC-6 and §1.4's Q8 clause. DC-10 governs the card's selectivity decision procedure.

5. Exempting the selectivity embeddings costs nothing the charter intends. AI-4 is never used for credit. The lock family is AI-1, the credit family and the lock fibers. B-SEL content is scored by §15.1. The pool-(b) reciprocity holdouts keep their explicit Q1 failure clause.
verdict.final_wording:
§3.1 Q1, append after the first sentence (leave the existing text unchanged):

"Exception: Q1 is not evaluated on the selectivity embeddings Emb(Σ). These are the §15.1 B-SEL items, the §15.9 pool-(a) holdouts (SEL-H), and pool-(a) items that have joined the public battery for a later card. Their protocols are measurement contexts with no a₀, and their records use the scenario's discrete alphabet. They are scored for selectivity by §15.1. The exception is from Q1 only, and it never covers AI-1, AI-2, AI-3, AI-5, a credit instance or a lock fiber. Every other rule that names these embeddings or applies to every in-domain instance still applies to them, including KU-1 to KU-3, KU-5 and §15.8, DC-8, BU-4(b), G4-NR, DIF-1 and DIF-7. On every other in-domain instance, a ⊥ or undefined coordinate of Im(ι) is a Q1 failure."

finding.clause: §3.3 MC-6 and MC-11 (Intake pre-assessment), with Appendix G items 2, 4, 6, 8 and 9
finding.quote: 9. The protocol acts on the environment only through the system; no actuator heating, EMI, vibration or other cross-talk. … 6. … the record contains the full support of every interface kernel, past and future

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute the defect and could not. Nothing else in the charter puts a tolerance on Appendix G items 2-9, and several clauses push toward the literal, absolute reading.

1. **The checklist must be passed and is pre-assessed at intake.** MC-6 requires the platform to pass the frozen checklist. MC-11 has the Intake auditor pre-assess every item as satisfiable, or the card is CARD-UNMEASURABLE at S7. G5-LOCK re-applies MC-6, and a failed certification counts as LOCK-FALSIFIED.

2. **No other clause supplies a tolerance.**
   - BP-4's "judged at charter resolution" and δ_RH apply to regime hypotheses only.
   - MC-3 and MC-5 (σ_pre "systematics included", LOCK-VOID above 1.25σ_pre) assume nonzero systematics. They never qualify the wording of Appendix G.
   - Item 1 has an explicit tolerance. Under CV-1, that makes its absence from items 2-9 read as deliberate.

3. **Other clauses block every fallback.**
   - The card cannot set a tolerance (CV-6).
   - The kit could fix constants under CV-6, but tolerances for this checklist are not in the §19.3 scope or in G2-12's (a)-(d) list. Under §19.3, anything the kit cannot do takes the hostile default.
   - DC-3 makes a tolerance-based "≈ 0" UNSCORABLE unless the tolerance is frozen.
   - DC-6 says an UNSCORABLE mandatory item fails the gate.
   - Measurement can certify only a bound, never exact zero. So "no cross-talk" (item 9), "protocol-independent" (items 2 and 4) and "no gains beyond the model" (item 3) cannot be certified on any physical platform.

4. **Item 6.** R1 (R1_T_LADDER, record completeness) treats kernel memory outside the grid as mode selection. "At driver resolution" sets how the record is sampled, not how far a kernel reaches. An exponential tail is nonzero at every grid point, including before the record starts.

5. **Item 8 is worse than reported.** Any digitized continuous record is ADC-quantized, and that quantization is never "provably inactive". So item 8 fails on P-1 and P-3 as well as on P-2 counts.

So every card fails S7 and SC3 cannot be reached. That makes this a BLOCKER of the too-strict kind, which falls inside CR-1's scope.

**Side note, outside this finding.** §1.4 computes ε "on continuous records", which may separately strand P-2 count platforms.

**What a correct fix needs.**
- A tolerance only on the clauses that are physical magnitudes.
- Exact readings kept on the design clauses, which can be met exactly by building the apparatus that way.
- The tolerance tied to the carrier, MODE SELECTION and T-tier verdicts the checklist exists to protect, and to the inputs of J_K, not only to the lock observables.
verdict.fix_problems:
1. **It loosens design clauses that can be met exactly.** The fix covers every absolute in items 2-9. That includes item 5 (one channel, fixed weights, no push-pull reweighting), item 7 (no vetoes, cuts or lock-loss rejection), and the fixed grid, trigger phase and window in item 4. These are mode-selection and selection-bias mechanisms. Turning them into effect bounds admits outcome-dependent cuts and protocol-indexed reweighting. Their effect also cannot be bounded without the records, which conflicts with MC-2 (certification independent of the records used to test ℛ★) and with MC-6 (never revised with lock data).

2. **The tolerance is tied only to the lock observables.** R1 §7 shows that an artefact such as protocol-dependent readout noise can fire Tier 1 on an exogenous environment. It can do so, and flip a carrier or MODE SELECTION verdict, or shift route-(i) or route-(ii) inputs to J_K, while barely moving the lock observable. The certification would pass while the identification is false.

3. **The tolerance is per item with no sum.** Eight items at σ_pre/Q_min each are not required to fit inside σ_pre.

4. **The kernel-support rule has two problems.**
   - It uses an undefined "BL-norm weight". Under CV-1 that ambiguity goes against the card, which reinstates the kill.
   - It sets a fixed 2^(−p★) (about 1e-3) relative tail weight that is not tied to witness size. R1 witnesses can be about 1e-6 (item 1 for BRI1), and kernel memory outside the grid is exactly R1's mode-selection mechanism.

5. **"Discrete by its declared type" lets the card exempt itself.** A declaration would exempt the thresholding or discrimination map that turns the detector signal into counts, which is the non-invertible quantization item 8 targets.

6. **It conflicts with MC-6's blinding.** MC-6 requires the checklist to be completed by an agent blind to the observable. That agent cannot propagate effects to the lock observables. Certifying the raw bounds and propagating them must be split between two roles.

7. **It does not require the bounds to come from interface-side calibration data only (MC-2).**

finding.quote: meets {ε > r_lock}, and meets the region where the card's Π is realized.
finding.problem:
This condition binds every relation, including SCOPE-G relations, whose lock observables are response functionals.
- For those observables r_lock = max(2σ_pre, 2^(−p★)·|W|), in the functional's own units, with W its range over B-HB. Whenever r_lock ≥ 2 the set {ε > r_lock} is empty, because ε ≤ 2.
- On fibers where standard theory gives 𝒜_ε = {0} (RH-KMS with RH-GAU and linear coupling, STD-3), the set is empty for any r_lock.

Addition 4 created SCOPE-G as 'response in general' precisely because ε is blind to linear response. As written, a scope-G card fails SC1 (CARD-UNINFORMATIVE at S6) with no defect in its relation. CHARTER TEST pattern: a SCOPE-G relation whose lock fiber is a linear-Gaussian platform.
finding.fix_wording: "… and the excluded set FB ∖ Z(ℛ★) has nonempty relative interior in FB (positive reference measure on discrete parts), meets, for a SCOPE-Q relation, {ε^{T_Π} > r_lock of its ε observable}, and meets the region where the card's Π is realized."

verdict.fix_problems:
Limiting the guard to SCOPE-Q is correct, and on its own it opens no loophole. Two parts of the proposed wording are flawed:

1. **"r_lock of its ε observable" can name nothing.** MC-1 lets a scope-Q relation lock "a frozen witness whose value ℛ★ fixes" rather than ε. Such a card has no ε observable.
   - Under CV-1 this ambiguity is read against the card, which creates a new hidden kill for scope-Q cards locked on a witness.
   - Read generously instead, the guard vanishes for those cards, which is a loophole.
   - Either way it is new wording the defect does not need.

2. **Writing ε^{T_Π} changes scope-Q meaning beyond what the defect requires.** It sits badly with G2-12 item 6, which CR-1 is to apply. Under that item, when T_Π is injective in Π, ℛ★ is stated at a catalogue class (default T_mono) and "T_Π enters through generation gates only". A guard at T_Π would then be misaligned with the relation, and might be stricter than intended where ε^{T_Π} = 0 holds widely.

The minimal repair adds only the scope qualifier, with RS-4 reclassification taken into account. It leaves the frozen ε and r_lock wording unchanged for scope Q; any remaining scope-Q ambiguity about which class or which r_lock is a separate item (it also affects Q9). The reported fix also omits RS-4; without it, it is unclear whether the scope as declared or as reclassified governs.

finding.problem:

- Weak coupling: transplant draws are B-HB models at generic coupling under the reference measure, with couplings ∈ [0, 1]. verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. Read as a whole, the charter still kills an honest card here.

1. Q3(c) as frozen (lines 698-713) counts every scorable draw. Nothing removes uninformative ones. Draws are B-HB models 'under H' with couplings in [0,1] (§15.4, App. A) under 'the reference measure'. That measure is log-uniform on default ranges per §1.5 AI-3, which is the assumption m11 made. Even a uniform measure on [0,1] leaves the problem.

2. Possible rescues fail:
- 𝔐_std(ι|H) (§2.2) admits any model that satisfies H's constraints, so weakly coupled models are 'under H'.
- BP-7 lets the Evaluator enlarge the transplant families.
- BP-4's hostile default usually keeps RH-WC in H.
- Even where RH-WC is certified to fail by δ_RH = 3·r̂_lock, a surrogate linear in the coupling still admits draws whose g^k-scaled observables are far below r_lock.
- Q9 and MC-4 constrain the lock fiber, not the draws.
- The CR-1 repair for NR-4 (G2-12 item 5) is scoped to NR-4. NR-4 borrows only Q3(c)'s threshold ('the transplant threshold of Q3(c)'), not an exclusion.

3. A rough estimate shows the corner is large. Take a relation ε^{T_Π} = F(u), where F vanishes as a dynamical interface statistic vanishes (single-model rule). Back-reaction at order g^k (STD-15) falls below r_lock = max(2σ_pre, 2^(−10)|W|) at quite large couplings. For example, k = 4 and r_lock ≈ 0.1 put the threshold near g ≈ 0.5. That alone exceeds 1/Q_min = 10% of draws under either measure, and the result is terminal S5 CARD-STANDARD for a relation whose content lies at nontrivial coupling. This is exactly the m11 mechanism the owner accepted for NR-4.

4. NR-17(b) has the same exposure, but it is weaker because its threshold is 90%. Trivial decoupled-corner agreement inflates the fraction of Sol(𝒦₂) that satisfies ℛ★.

5. A side observation, not reported: a scope-Q relation must predict ε = 0 under RH-GAU with linear coupling (RS-3). If Gaussian or exogenous HB draws (HB-1, HB-3, HB-4) count as 'under H', they always agree with ℛ★. The corrected exclusion below also removes those agreements.

6. On tolerance: the transplant test's r_lock moves with σ_pre. But the Q3(a) witnesses also use the lock scale (3·r_lock), and once the exclusion uses the same tolerance as the test, a noisier platform no longer enlarges the trivial corner. Decoupling Q3(c)'s own tolerance from σ_pre is not needed for this defect, and doing so would loosen the test beyond the corner.

Severity is MAJOR, not BLOCKER: the kill depends on the form of the relation, but it hits a natural class of honest relations and cannot be loosened after Card 1 (§19.2).
verdict.fix_problems:
The proposed fix, as worded, has four problems.

(1) The replacement is unbounded and the test can go vacuous. 'Replaced by further draws' has no cap, which breaks DC-1 termination. It can also hollow out Q3(c): if the card's components send nearly every standard draw to decoupled lock values, almost every draw is excluded and the half-scorable rule never fires. An example is an X_T that, on standard models, returns a class at which ε ≡ 0 while ℛ★ predicts 0 there. This is the CT-69 pipeline tautology, and the frozen text catches it (90% of draws satisfy, so CARD-STANDARD). The fix would exclude all of those draws and pass the card.

(2) The decoupling check depends on the card's own components. Whether a draw is 'within r_lock of its decoupled value' is judged with the card's components on that draw, so the card can push strongly coupled draws into the excluded set. The check must use the card's fixed, realized lock-fiber interface instead.

(3) The exclusion also removes informative violations. Excluding on lock observables alone removes draws whose observables sit at decoupled values but violate ℛ★ (ℛ★ predicts a value away from decoupling). Those draws are evidence for the card. Removing them from the denominator raises the satisfied fraction, which is a new tightening in Q3(c) and NR-17(b). Only trivially satisfying draws should leave.

(4) The tolerance cross-reference is ambiguous and points forward. 'Here within r_lock uses the in-silico tolerance CR-1 adopts for NR-4' refers to a tolerance CR-1 has not yet defined, and the fix does not say which tolerance it changes.
- If it changes only the exclusion tolerance, and that tolerance is smaller than r_lock, draws between the two tolerances still satisfy ℛ★ trivially within r_lock, so the noisy-platform kill survives.
- If it changes the whole clause, it loosens Q3(c) beyond the corner (relations that standard models reproduce within σ_pre would pass) and puts Q3(c) out of step with Q3(a)'s 3·r_lock.

The fix: the exclusion must use the same tolerance as the test it modifies.

On NR-17(b): reusing NR-4's definition of the S–E-decoupled value is fine there. It needs a non-vacuity guard, and that guard can never fire for a card whose lock-fiber solutions are nontrivial.

An excluded draw still counts as scorable. It is replaced by a further post-freeze draw, up to 10·N draws in all, where N is the number of committed draws. The excluded fraction is reported with the verdict. If fewer than N/2 scorable draws remain unexcluded, no draw is excluded."

finding.quote: the domain being a decidable predicate frozen in C16 that contains AI-1 and AI-2 … On AI-2 instances …, every solution carries a persistent, nontrivial, A-stable Π
finding.problem:
The Evaluator builds the AI-2 instances after freeze, with no restriction to the card's domain, yet the card's frozen predicate must contain them. NR-5 then requires a persistent, nontrivial Π on every solution of every such instance.

CHARTER TEST pattern: Π appears spontaneously on symmetric inputs, but only above a threshold of some instance parameter. If the Evaluator picks a symmetric instance below the threshold, the card fails NR-5 even though nothing there was supplied. CV-1 resolves the choice of AI-2 against the card, giving CARD-NONGENERATIVE at S3; Q1 and DIF-7 fail there as well. This kills every card whose differentiation exists only in part of its parameter space.
finding.fix_wording:
AI-2 row: "Symmetric-input instances satisfying the card's frozen domain predicate (C16): Aut(𝒞) transitive on V or on the candidate partitions."

DIF-7: "… a decidable predicate frozen in C16 that contains AI-1, admits transitive instances at every relata count from n_min to 2·n_min (AI-2 is drawn inside it), and covers ≥ θ_gen [A] of the AI-3 draws (priced, IP-13)."

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute the defect and could not. The frozen text does kill an honest card.

**How the kill works**
- §1.5 (line 386) says AI-2 instances are "Symmetric-input instances: Aut(𝒞) transitive on V or on the candidate partitions", generated by the Evaluator. Nothing restricts them to the card's domain, and nothing bounds their relata count.
- §18.1 step 3 has the Selector commit the AI-2 constructions after the card's freeze.
- DIF-7 as frozen (lines 2128-2130) requires the C16 predicate to *contain* AI-2. So the card has to accommodate whatever the Selector builds; it cannot exclude any of it.
- NR-5 (lines 1143-1155) requires that "every solution carries a persistent, nontrivial, A-stable Π" on AI-2 instances. Failing it means CARD-NONGENERATIVE, which is terminal at S3.
- Under CV-1 and CV-2, the Evaluator may choose a symmetric instance below threshold, or with fewer relata than n_min, for example n = 2 or 3. A card whose symmetry breaking needs a coupling or size threshold then fails, even though nothing there was supplied. That covers the standard spontaneous-differentiation mechanisms: Landau-type bifurcations, Turing patterns, and mean-field symmetry breaking.

**Rescues I checked**
1. *Narrowing the type of 𝒞.* This does not work. The AI-3 measure is log-uniform on the charter's default ranges ([10⁻³, 10³], Appendix A), and C16's domain predicate (priced under IP-13) is the designated place for restrictions. Only cards whose numeric data are all law constants, and that break symmetry at every size, escape.
2. *NR-5's "λ = 0 (if in the domain)".* This shows the drafters expected domain-relative probing. But it conflicts with the AI-2 row and with DIF-7's "contains AI-2", and CV-1 resolves that conflict against the card.
3. *§5.5 STRONG wording.* "NR-5 passes on a transitive instance" could suggest passing per instance. Under CV-1 the strict reading (every AI-2 instance) governs.
4. *NR-5 Generalization.* "a G-invariant input must still yield some persistent X" is unqualified, so under CV-1 it kills the same card on its own.

This is a hidden kill, inside G2-12's CR-1 scope, and cannot be loosened once Card 1 is drafted.
verdict.fix_problems:
The proposed fix restricts AI-2 to the domain predicate, and the companion DIF-7 text requires transitive instances at every relata count from n_min to 2·n_min. Five problems remain.

(1) **Conditioning loophole.** Symmetric instances have essentially zero mass under the AI-3 reference measure, so excluding them costs nothing in θ_gen coverage, and IP-13 then charges only L_stmt(predicate). A card could therefore exclude exactly the symmetric and near-symmetric instances at parameters where its law fails to break symmetry, while keeping the asymmetric instances at those same parameters in its domain. On those instances Π merely tracks the input asymmetry. NR-6 and NR-7 fire only at p_dec = 0.5, so such a region can be up to about 49% of the domain. The honest card instead excludes the whole sub-threshold region. Nothing in the fix tells these two apart.

(2) **Vacuous pass at S3.** The companion requirement sits in DIF-7, which is a Stage-4 gate run on the picked card only. A domain with no transitive instance therefore passes NR-5 vacuously at S3 and gets an unpriced GENERATED-WEAK, instead of the IP-7 pricing NR-5 applies when 𝒞's type cannot be symmetric.

(3) **New hidden kill.** "At every relata count" kills types that have no transitive instance at some n, for example 3-regular graphs at odd n.

(4) **Incomplete.** The NR-5 Generalization ("a G-invariant input must still yield some persistent X") is unchanged, so under CV-1 it still kills the honest threshold card.

(5) **Conflict.** Frozen DIF-7's "contains AI-2" is left as is.

**Residual after my wording.** If 𝒞 has only discrete data, there is no zero-average perturbation, so a predicate could still admit only "easy" (imprimitive) transitive structures at composite n. This is bounded: an AI-2 instance is required at every n from n_min to 2·n_min or the card is priced, and by Bertrand's postulate there is a prime n in that range, where a transitive instance has a primitive group and so no nontrivial Aut-invariant partition. Suitable for the CR-2 queue.
verdict.final_wording:
§1.5, AI-2 row. Content: "Symmetric-input instances inside the frozen domain predicate (C16): Aut(𝒞) transitive on V or on the candidate partitions. A transitive instance that the predicate excludes is also an AI-2 instance, with NR-5 run there in full (λ = 0 included), if the predicate admits some instance obtained from it by a perturbation of 𝒞's numeric data whose average over Aut(𝒞) is zero." Generated by: "The Evaluator (constructions committed by the Selector, §18.1)".

§5.3 NR-5, Generalization: "… a G-invariant input that is in the domain, or that the domain excludes while admitting a perturbation of it whose average over G is zero, must still yield some persistent X up to 𝒦's own symmetry; …". Replace the sentence beginning "If 𝒞's type cannot be symmetric" with: "If 𝒞's type cannot be symmetric, or there is no AI-2 instance at some relata count from n_min to 2·n_min, its asymmetry is priced under IP-7 as a supplied commitment, NR-6 and NR-7 apply at full strength, and Π cannot be GENERATED-STRONG."

§15.10 DIF-7: "… the domain being a decidable predicate frozen in C16 that contains AI-1 and covers ≥ θ_gen [A] of the AI-3 draws (priced, IP-13); AI-2 is drawn under it (§1.5); …"

finding.clause: §1.3 Persistent and A-stable, and Horizon; Appendix A δ_Π / η / δ_∂ (DIF-2)
finding.quote: the reassigned fraction is ≤ η [A], with ∂ counted as reassigned … δ_Π / η / δ_∂ | 0.05 / 0.05 / 0.10 … H_hor ≥ max(protocol and record window, 10·τ_int, 3·τ_slow)
finding.problem:
(a) Thresholds at audit sizes. Credit and AI-3 instances have 8–16 relata.
- One reassigned or boundary relatum is a fraction of at least 1/16 = 0.0625 > η.
- Moving one relatum gives VI_norm ≥ 0.114 at n = 16 and 0.256 at n = 8 (computed), both > δ_Π.
So Π must be exactly crisp and exactly invariant at every protocol and time. δ_∂ and the whole approximate-Π machinery (∂, the persistent core, PC-7(d), STD-13's 'relaxation of ∂') can never be used. This kills every card whose generated Π has any boundary or one fluctuating relatum.

(b) The horizon. τ_slow is taken 'within the conserved sector'. For a finite stochastic law with metastable differentiation, that includes the escape time from the differentiated state, so H_hor ≥ 3·τ_slow outlasts the differentiation itself. NR-5 (with PC-3 covariance) rules out a unique invariant state on symmetric inputs. Every finite-size stochastic card whose Π is metastable, rather than exactly non-ergodic, therefore fails DIF-2.
finding.fix_wording:
Replace the reassignment bullet: "the reassigned fraction is ≤ max(η, 1/|V|), with ∂ counted as reassigned, and |∂|/|V| ≤ max(δ_∂, 1/|V|)." Add to both VI_norm bullets: "or the two partitions differ only by the reassignment of at most max(⌊η·|V|⌋, 1) relata."

Horizon: "… τ_slow is the slowest relaxation time within the conserved or metastable sector of the realized reference state. The escape modes out of that sector are excluded if the card proves that the mean escape time exceeds Q_min·H_hor on every lock-fiber and credit instance; otherwise τ_slow includes them."

verdict.reasoning:
Part (a) is real. Part (b) is not.

(a) The arithmetic checks out (I recomputed it). Appendix A fixes n_min = 8, so AI-3 and credit instances have 8 to 16 relata. At those sizes η·|V| is between 0.4 and 0.8, so the η bullet (§1.3, with ∂ counted as reassigned) allows no reassigned relatum and no boundary relatum. The smallest nonzero VI_norm is a one-relatum move: 0.256 at n=8 and 0.114 at n=16, and it stays above δ_Π = 0.05 up to n ≈ 32 (n ≈ 43 for balanced blocks). So both VI bullets require Π to be exactly invariant across protocols and t ≤ H_hor.

δ_∂ = 0.10 can never bind at any size, because ∂ already counts against η = 0.05. At audit sizes the approximate-Π assignment, the persistent core and the PC-7(d) ablation are all empty.

No other clause rescues the card:
- DIF-7 makes Π universal on all of Sol on every in-domain instance.
- The domain must contain AI-1 and AI-2 and at least 90% of AI-3 draws.
- Dom_gate needs persistence.
- The b_J minimum runs over all of I_𝒦.
- CV-1 resolves ambiguities against the card.

Lock fibers may be large, but the credit family cannot be. So a card whose generated Π has a single boundary or fluctuating relatum on more than 10% of draws fails, even though §1.3 explicitly invites approximate Π. This is the infeasible-arithmetic and hidden-kill type that G2-12 puts in CR-1. One overstatement in the report: the machinery is dead at audit sizes, not "never" usable, since it still works on large lock fibers.

(b) As written, τ_slow does include the escape time for a finite ergodic stochastic law. But this is deliberate, not hidden:
- RT-13 ("Persistence by horizon choice: a Π that is only an unrelaxed imprint of initial data, or of a slow mode") introduced the 3·τ_slow bound for exactly this case.
- The fallback "Π must be shown invariant under the realized stationary dynamics" states the intent: exact persistence.
- The "conserved sector" phrase (F-14/O-6) was added only to cure τ_slow = ∞.
- DC-4 says claims about the limit earn nothing, and metastability with escape times that diverge in the large-size limit is such a claim.
- NR-5 and Q1 ("every solution" / "all of Sol") already exclude an ergodic law whose Sol contains the symmetric stationary process.
- Honest classes remain: deterministic attractors, conserved sectors and absorbing classes. ST-6 can be completed favourably within them.

Admitting metastable Π would be a policy loosening for the owner, not a too-strict repair.
verdict.fix_problems:
1. The VI waiver "at most max(⌊η·|V|⌋, 1) relata" is too broad. The η bullet already caps the union of reassigned relata at η|V|, so the waiver makes both δ_Π bullets redundant to η at every size below about 730 relata, lock fibers included. There δ_Π is a real bound, not a granularity artifact. Computed worst cases that would newly pass: VI_norm 0.090 at n=40 (2 relata), 0.072 at n=100 (5), 0.062 at n=200 (10), all against δ_Π = 0.05. A one-relatum floor is enough: a single move falls below δ_Π by itself above about n=32 (n≈43 for balanced blocks).

2. The fix leaves horizon doubling at 2η (B-DIF (iv) and DIF-2). At n=8 and 9, 2η·|V| < 1, so the doubled-horizon test still forbids the relatum the base test now allows. Those instances are not rescued.

3. Non-vacuity interaction. At small n a one-relatum move counts as a relevant variable (it exceeds δ_Π). Once such a move is also tolerated as noise, a FROZEN core plus one token wobbling relatum passes both tests (CT-80 pattern). At large n this cannot happen, because a one-relatum move is below δ_Π there. Fix: exclude only the newly admitted relata from the relevant-variable test. No status-quo card is affected, so nothing is tightened.

4. The horizon rewrite reopens RT-13. "Metastable sector" is undefined, so any slow mode separated by Q_min from the rest can be declared a sector and dropped from τ_slow, and the escape-time proof is the card's own. That is exactly RT-13's "unrelaxed imprint of a slow mode". It also contradicts the fallback "invariant under the realized stationary dynamics".

5. The line-241 bound |∂|/|V| ≤ δ_∂ also needs the floor, for n=8 and 9.

Residual for the owner, out of this defect's scope: the scale window and DIF-6 ("within δ_Π") are also exact at audit sizes. A 1/|V| floor there could let a tuned threshold decide one unablated relatum, so it belongs in a separate item or the CR-2 queue, not in this repair.
verdict.final_wording:
§1.3, approximate Π: replace "|∂|/|V| ≤ δ_∂ [A]" with "|∂|/|V| ≤ max(δ_∂, 1/|V|) [A]".

§1.3, third persistence bullet: "the reassigned fraction is ≤ max(η, 1/|V|) [A], with ∂ counted as reassigned;"

Add after that bullet:
"**Granularity allowance.** In the two VI_norm bullets, two partitions that differ only by the reassignment of a single relatum, with no block of either left empty, also count as within δ_Π. That relatum counts as reassigned: it is outside the persistent core and in the PC-7(d) ablation set. A variable whose change moves only relata admitted only by the 1/|V| floors or by this allowance is not a relevant variable (non-vacuous bullet)."

§15.7(iv) and Appendix A ("Horizon; robustness; scale window" row): replace "(2η, 2·H_hor)" with "(max(2η, 1/|V|), 2·H_hor), with the §1.3 granularity allowance".

Horizon clause (§1.3; Appendix A): no change.

I tried to refute the report and could not. The defect is real and it is a too-strict kill.

1. What the controls are. C2-F (R1/c2_controls.py) is F_a = K_a·ξ with a protocol-dependent causal exponential filter K_a (τ = 0.05 vs 0.20). These are lower-triangular, unit-diagonal maps that mix time. C2-F′ (D5_evidence/c2nm/markov_checks.py) is the same construction with two-exponential filters, again different per protocol. D5 calls it "still one GL(k) orbit".

2. What the charter requires. §15.3 requires exactly 0 at T_Π for "C2-F′, … HB-5 with calibrated filters". HB-5 is defined in §15.4 as covering both C2-F and C2-F′. The second sentence lists C2-F′ again, with no qualifier, for the E-relatum run. DIF-5(e) requires ε^{T_Π} = 0 on every exogenous control listed in §15.3.
   - The B-REC procedure removes only the static tail. No clause removes calibrated filters before ε is taken.
   - The table row "C2-F′ | 0" has no class attached.
   - Result: any T_Π that does not contain the protocol filters fails. That covers E₂±, T_mono and every coordinatewise class.

3. Why rescue readings fail.
   - (a) One could read "HB-5 with calibrated filters" as "with the filters added to T". But C2-F′ is listed bare, so the kill remains even under that reading.
   - (b) R1's rule that calibrated filters are "removed with their known maps", and NR-10(k)'s apparatus layer, are not in the B-REC procedure. §19.3 says HB-5 is zero "under T_lin", which shows the zero is meant to depend on the class.
   - (c) Under CV-1 any ambiguity goes against the card anyway.

4. Why an honest card is killed. §1.4 allows T_Π = T_mono ("a result to be proved"). G2-12 item 6 names T_mono as the default class. SCOPE-Q requires only T_Π ⊇ E₂±, and its kit check (HB-1, HB-3, HB-4, Gaussian families) deliberately leaves out HB-5. A card whose generated T_Π is T_mono or another coordinatewise class therefore fails three ways:
   - T_Π is not GENERATED (§5.5);
   - every ε^{T_Π} relation fails Q8 at S5;
   - G4-DIF fails.

   The class is legitimate, so the rule is too strict. It is in CR-1 scope and must be fixed before Card 1. It is MAJOR rather than BLOCKER because cards with T_Π ⊇ T_caus pass.

5. Side note. C2-G and C2-NG (HB-3, HB-4) apply only per-time affine maps, as WO-001 specifies, so they are zero at any T_Π ⊇ E₂±. Keeping them strict is correct. The kit must not build C2-G with protocol-dependent filters, an option the c2_controls docstring raises.

1. "T_Π extended by the calibrated filters" is not in 𝕃_T^adm and has no valid s_T. By §1.4, an ε value taken at such a class is void. For T_Π = T_mono, the group generated by T_mono and K_a lies inside J and may trivialize as R1 expects J to; ε at J is void by rule (CT-14). This leaves two outcomes, both bad:
   - The required value cannot be certified. Under CV-1 the honest card still fails, so the fix does not fix the problem.
   - If someone computes it anyway, the enlarged group can absorb almost anything. The HB-5 E-relatum check of the card's static maps (PC-7(b), CT-93) then becomes vacuous: a card could pass HB-5 with a static nonlinearity that should create ε. That is a mild loophole, since HB-3 and HB-4 still test static maps.
2. "at T_Π itself only if T_Π contains those filters" is redundant: when T_Π contains the filters, the extension adds nothing.
3. The fix leaves two places untouched that bring the kill back under CV-1:
   - the second §15.3 sentence still lists C2-F′ separately;
   - the B-REC table row still reads "C2-F′ | 0" with no class.

The better route is R1's own rule: remove the calibrated filters with their known maps, then evaluate at T_Π. When T_Π contains the filters, the requirement stays as strict as before. For other T_Π, the record-level part becomes trivial. The static-map test keeps its force: K_a⁻¹Σφ(K_aξ_i) still differs between protocols for a nonlinear φ. For any static maps that commute with the filters (for example, time-local linear maps) it gives zero.
verdict.final_wording:

finding.quote: If the auditor cannot find enough in-scope classes, G5-HOLD fails. At most one holdout may be replaced by a prospective experiment
finding.problem:
G5-HOLD needs at least max(2, n_obs) holdouts, and at least one of them must be existing measured data on a different physical class. The lock observables are chart coordinates at the frozen templates: ramps of ±α (1 SD of the driven S variable) starting at t₁ = H_hor/4, where H_hor is the card's own horizon.

For a SCOPE-Q relation (T_Π-invariant witnesses of per-protocol record laws), no archived dataset can contain those card-specific protocols, so the required archived holdout cannot exist. In addition, a shortfall in the hostile auditor's search is charged to the card, whereas §15.9 and T-3(b) give an auditor-side void one reselection.

Every scope-Q card that passes G5-LOCK then fails Stage 5, and T-3(b) terminates the route. Under §19.2 this can no longer be loosened once the first 𝒦 draft is logged.
finding.fix_wording: Replace the two sentences with: "Any holdout may be a prospective experiment the hostile auditor designs or approves (protocol committed by hash before any data exist; unsealed within T_lock of G5-LOCK). G5-HOLD fails for lack of holdouts only if fewer than max(2, n_obs) in-scope classes admit archived data or a prospective experiment feasible under MC-7 and MC-11."

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute it and could not.

1. At least one archived dataset is required. G5-HOLD needs max(2, n_obs) holdouts, which is 2 or 3. It says "measured data only" and "At most one holdout may be replaced by a prospective experiment". Any new measurement is prospective by MC-8's own definition (LOCK-E: "protocol committed before any data exist"), so at least one holdout, two when n_obs = 3, must come from pre-existing data. Even if someone argued for a looser reading, CV-1 resolves ambiguity against the card.

2. That data cannot realistically exist for a scope-Q card. MC-1 makes a scope-Q lock observable a T-invariant witness, and the §1.5 chart defines those coordinates "on the template grid". Ch-2 freezes the templates. Appendix A fixes them as linear ramps of ±α and 2α starting at t₁ = H_hor/4, where α is 1 SD under a₀ of the card's generated driven S variable and H_hor is the card's own C7 horizon. Under MC-5, a change of protocol set or grid is LOCK-VOID, and holdouts are judged by MC-5's confirmation condition. An archived dataset from an unreferenced physical class that drives that generated variable with exactly those ramps is, for practical purposes, impossible. Scope Q also excludes mean and linear response, so substitute data cannot stand in. The report's "no archived dataset can" is slightly too strong; "practically never" is accurate, and the effect is the same.

3. No other clause rescues the card.
- MC-8's LOCK-E fallback covers only the lock.
- §15.9's auditor-side void covers its pools (a)–(d). G5-HOLD is not one of them, and its own sentence ("G5-HOLD fails") is specific and overrides the general rule.
- T-3(b) then counts the failure.
- G2-12 item 4 accepts scope Q unchanged as a legitimate route, so this rule kills honest cards for a reason unrelated to whether the law is true. That is squarely within CR-1's too-strict mandate.
- Under §19.2 it cannot be loosened after the first draft.

4. The red-team record (RT-12) shows that "at most one" was added to stop authors replacing holdouts with their own preregistered experiment. The added "hostile auditor designs or approves" guard already does that job, so the cap is not needed for its stated purpose.

5. The second sub-claim, that a search shortfall is charged to the card, is weaker. If the declared scope is too narrow, that is fairly the card's fault. But "cannot find" ties the verdict to how hard the auditor searched rather than to what classes exist, so an objective test is better.

MAJOR rather than BLOCKER: Stage-3 admissibility and scope-G cards are unaffected. What it kills is the whole scope-Q route at Stage 5, and that cannot be undone later.
verdict.fix_problems:
The proposed fix does not let a card pass without the intended content: every holdout still needs MC-5 confirmation on sealed measured data, and classes are still chosen by the hostile auditor. It does have these problems:

(a) It sets a T_lock deadline for prospective holdouts but no consequence for missing it. With every holdout possibly prospective, a card whose experiments are never run never passes and never fails G5-HOLD. T-3(b) can then never fire and the route stalls. That contradicts T-2 (no OPEN terminal) and MC-8's parallel rule ("or G5-LOCK fails"). The original wording has the same gap for its single prospective holdout; the fix extends it to every holdout.

(b) "Feasible under MC-7" is ambiguous. MC-7's limits are per card (10^9 effective records and 30 days of platform time per card). Read cumulatively across the lock and several holdouts, they bring back a hidden kill. The fix should say the limits apply to each holdout separately.

(c) Nothing stops a hostile auditor from designing an underpowered experiment. That gives σ_eff > |J_K|/4, so MC-5 cannot confirm and the card fails for an auditor-side reason. The fix should require at least the N_req that MC-7 gives for that holdout.

(d) In the failure test, "archived data" is not restricted to the frozen templates and grid. A class with unusable archived data would count as "admitting" a holdout, which blocks a lack-of-holdouts failure but supplies no usable holdout, so the gate stalls again.

(e) Minor: "unsealed within T_lock" should not depend on a platform class that MC-11 marks as LOCK-H only. Naming MC-11 as the platform condition handles this.
verdict.final_wording:
In §15.11 G5-HOLD, replace the sentences "If the auditor cannot find enough in-scope classes, G5-HOLD fails. At most one holdout may be replaced by a prospective experiment the hostile auditor designs or approves." with:

"Any holdout may be a prospective experiment the hostile auditor designs or approves, on a platform meeting MC-11, run with at least the N_req that MC-7 gives for that holdout (MC-7's limits applied to each holdout separately), with its protocol committed by hash before any data exist; it is unsealed within T_lock of G5-LOCK, or G5-HOLD fails. G5-HOLD fails for lack of holdouts only if fewer than max(2, n_obs) in-scope classes admit either archived data at the frozen templates and grid or such an experiment; a shortfall in the auditor's search alone is an auditor-side void (one disclosed reselection, T-3(b))."

finding.clause: §3.3 MC-4 (live rival) with MC-7 (feasibility) and MC-9 (z_obs); App. A lock thresholds
finding.quote: strictly more than 3σ_pre outside J_K; power (MC-7) is computed against the nearest such rival
finding.problem:
A live rival qualifies once it lies just beyond 3σ_pre from J_K. MC-9, however, raises falsification to dist > z_obs·σ_eff, with σ_eff = max(σ_pre, σ_stat) ≥ σ_pre and z_obs = 3.32, 3.51 or 3.62.

For a rival at distance d, with 3σ_pre < d < z_obs·σ_pre, the measured value converges to d as N grows. Power at the α_obs threshold therefore never reaches 0.9 (computed, n_obs = 1: d = 3.2σ_pre gives power ≤ 0.45 at every N; d = 3.05σ_pre gives ≤ 0.39). Even at the old threshold 3σ_eff, a rival at 3σ_pre + δ needs N ∝ 1/δ².

Standard witnesses consistent with the BP-5 inputs form continuous families. MC-4 also forces J_SRB to be at least 10 times wider than J_K ⊕ 2σ_tot. So under CV-1 the Evaluator can always exhibit a verified rival arbitrarily close to 3σ_pre. Then N_req = ∞ > N_max, and every card that passes MC-4 is CARD-UNMEASURABLE at S7, so SC3 is unreachable.

The round-1 m-14 edit fixed only the wording 'strictly more than'.
finding.fix_wording:
MC-4, replace the sentence after the live-rival clause with: "Power (MC-7) is computed against a rival placed at d★ := max(d_near, (z_obs + 2)·σ_pre) outside J_K, on the side of the nearest live rival, where d_near is the infimum distance of the live rivals from J_K."

The MC-5 falsification and confirmation rules are unchanged, and LOCK-INCONCLUSIVE remains a G5-LOCK fail. A world sitting at a near-boundary rival therefore still cannot confirm the card, so this opens no loophole.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute the defect and could not. No other clause fixes it.

1. **The arithmetic holds.** MC-5 and MC-9 set falsification at dist(O_meas, J_K) > z_obs·σ_eff, with σ_eff = max(σ_pre, σ_stat) ≥ σ_pre. In MC-7's in-silico simulation, O_meas ~ N(d, σ_stat²) for a rival at distance d. The cutoff never falls below z_obs·σ_pre. If 3σ_pre < d < z_obs·σ_pre, the mean sits below the cutoff for every N, so power stays under 0.5. I recomputed the maximum over all σ_stat/σ_pre:
   - n_obs = 1 (z = 3.32): 0.394 at d = 3.05σ_pre and 0.452 at d = 3.2σ_pre, matching the report.
   - n_obs = 2: 0.323 and 0.379.
   - n_obs = 3: 0.286 and 0.339.
   
   Even under the old 3σ_eff cutoff, a rival at 3σ_pre + δ needs N ∝ 1/δ².

2. **The nearest rival is always just beyond 3σ_pre.**
   - The B-HB families have continuous parameter ranges: β, frequencies, couplings and quartic λ (§15.4, App. A). Consistency with measured BP-5 inputs leaves a continuum of witnesses.
   - J_SRB is the hull of witness predictions (§15.5). For B-SRB to PASS, J_K ⊉ J_SRB and J_K meets J_SRB. MC-4 makes J_SRB at least 10× the size of J_K ⊕ 2σ_tot.
   - A connected witness image therefore covers every distance from J_K out to far rivals. The infimum of live-rival distances is 3σ_pre, and "strictly more than" means no nearest rival is attained.
   - BP-7 lets the Evaluator enlarge standard families for witness draws. CV-1 and CV-2 settle the ambiguity against the card. MC-7 lets the larger of the card's and the Evaluator's N_req govern.
   - So the Evaluator exhibits a rival at 3σ_pre⁺, N_req = ∞ > N_max, the card is CARD-UNMEASURABLE at S7, and SC3 cannot be reached.

3. **Nothing else in the charter rescues the card.**
   - Shrinking σ_pre does not help, because the band scales with σ_pre.
   - The card's own C13 "live rival" does not govern: MC-4 says "nearest such rival", and MC-7 takes the larger N_req.
   - No other clause in §16, §18 or the S7 screen limits the rival choice.
   - This is a hidden kill: an honest card fails, which is within CR-1's too-strict scope. BLOCKER is right, because it hits every card.

4. **The proposed fix does not open a confirmation loophole.** MC-5 is unchanged. LOCK-CONFIRMED still needs dist ≤ 2σ_eff and σ_eff ≤ |J_K|/4. A standard world between 2σ_eff and z_obs·σ_eff ends LOCK-INCONCLUSIVE, which MC-5 counts as a G5-LOCK fail. Any false confirmation by a standard world inside 2σ_eff is already possible under the current text and is unchanged.

5. **Using a real witness adds no new kill.** MC-3 gives |J_K| ≥ 4σ_pre and σ_tot ≥ σ_pre. If J_SRB stayed within (z_obs+2)σ_pre of J_K in every coordinate, then per coordinate N(J_SRB)/N(J_K ⊕ 2σ_tot) ≤ (4 + 2·5.62)/(4 + 4) ≈ 1.905. Over up to 3 box coordinates that gives ≤ 6.9 < Q_min = 10. Passing MC-4 therefore guarantees a verified witness at least (z_obs+2)σ_pre from J_K in some coordinate. At that distance, power reaches 0.9 once σ_stat ≤ (z+2)/(z+1.28)·σ_pre ≈ 1.16σ_pre, so N_req is finite. Power is continuous in d, so the infimum problem does not return at this floor.
verdict.fix_problems:
The proposed fix opens no loophole: a world at a standard witness still cannot pass, because MC-5 is unchanged and LOCK-INCONCLUSIVE is a G5-LOCK fail. Its drafting has four problems:

(1) "A rival placed at d★" is a made-up rival, not a verified standard witness. MC-7 computes N_req by "simulating the frozen estimator ... on the live rival", so it needs a generative model to simulate. A made-up rival has none. Under CV-1, the Evaluator could pick the worst realization, which could make N_req as large as it likes and reopen a hostile kill.

(2) MC-7 still says "the live rival". Under CV-1, that can be read as the nearest live rival, which brings the original defect back. The two clauses are also in tension: MC-7 simulates a live rival, and the made-up rival is not one.

(3) The made-up rival lets a card pass MC-7 even when every real live rival lies in (3σ_pre, z_obs·σ_pre]. No standard world could then ever be falsified, so KU-12 could never fire. This is not a confirmation loophole, and MC-4's ratio of at least 10 makes the case almost impossible, but it gives the lock less force than tying power to a real witness.

(4) max(d_near, ·) and "on the side of the nearest live rival" are not needed. The nearest verified witness at or beyond the floor gives the same result whenever d_near is above the floor, and it is a real witness with a defined realization.

The +2 margin is acceptable. It mirrors the MC-5 confirmation multiplier. The minimum would be +Φ⁻¹(0.9) ≈ +1.28, and the two differ only by a constant factor in N_req. The existence threshold of 3σ_pre is left alone: raising it would be a tightening, which belongs in the CR-2 queue.
verdict.final_wording:
In §3.3 MC-4, replace "predicts the observable strictly more than 3σ_pre outside J_K; power (MC-7) is computed against the nearest such rival." with:

"predicts the observable strictly more than 3σ_pre outside J_K. The live rival that MC-7 simulates, and against which power is computed, is the nearest live rival whose prediction lies at least (z_obs + 2)·σ_pre outside J_K, with z_obs as in MC-9. Nearer live rivals are not used for power. MC-5 is unchanged."

finding.clause: §2.5 Realized coupling (product hull 𝓗; c_J(a); dim_lb by B-HB witnesses) and Q3(a)
finding.quote: U and R are the realized interface and response values over 𝓘, and the product hull is 𝓗 := FB ∩ (cl U × cl R)
finding.problem:
R consists of the card's realized response values in every frozen chart coordinate. The chart includes ε and every T-invariant functional at each catalogue class and at T_Π. At r★★ that is about 10³ invariant cumulant coordinates per protocol.

The requirements are:
- FB points must be realized by a single m ∈ 𝔐_std, i.e. B-HB families and their compositions, each with a few dozen parameters.
- dim_lb 𝓗 must be certified by B-HB witnesses on a box inside cl U × cl R.
- Q3(a) requires Obs(m*_F) ∈ 𝓗 ∖ Z(ℛ★).

All three demand that a B-HB model reproduce a realized response of the card exactly in every chart coordinate, including coordinates ℛ★ never reads. For a card whose full-chart response is not, coordinate for coordinate, a B-HB response (generically, any non-standard law), the following holds:
- 𝓗 is empty or low-dimensional, so c_J(a) ≤ 0 and Q5 fails (NONJOINT).
- No Q3(a) witness exists, so the constructive rule gives CARD-STANDARD.

CHARTER TEST pattern: a card whose relation couples one interface statistic to one response functional, while its other chart coordinates differ from every B-HB member, fails S5 whatever its relation is.
finding.fix_wording:
§2.5, replace the sentence with: "U and R are the realized interface values and the realized values of the ℛ★-coordinates (the chart coordinates read by ℛ★ or by a registered lock observable) over 𝓘. The product hull is 𝓗 := FB ∩ (cl U × cl R) in the coordinates (u, ℛ★-coordinates); each point of 𝓗 is still realized by a single m ∈ 𝔐_std(ι | H) (single-model rule)."

Q3(a), add: "Obs(m*_F) ∈ 𝓗 is read in the same coordinates."

Im, c_ι, c_J(b), the family cap, and the 'single-axis consequence' exclusion are unchanged.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute the defect and could not. Read as a whole, the text makes an honest card fail.

1. **What the text says.** §2.5 defines Im as the "full image of Sol in chart coordinates (u, r)". Here r is "frozen chart coordinates of Γ, with ε and every T-invariant functional evaluated at each catalogue class of 𝒯 and at T_Π". R is "the realized … response values over 𝓘", so R uses every chart response coordinate. At r★★ (k=4, d_rec=2, m≤5) that is on the order of 10³ cumulant coordinates; the exact count does not matter. FB points need a single m ∈ 𝔐_std (§2.2 single-model rule). 𝔐_std is the B-HB families and their compositions within the frozen ranges.

2. **Why both certificates require exact matches.** dim_lb must be certified by B-HB witnesses meeting the §15.4 witness rules. A Q3(a) witness needs Obs(m*_F) ∈ 𝓗 ∖ Z(ℛ★). Since Im ⊆ Z(ℛ★) by Q1, any point of 𝓗 ∖ Z is a cross pair (u₁, r₂). So the witness must be a B-HB model with interface u₁ that reproduces a realized card response r₂ exactly in every chart coordinate.

3. **Case: the card's responses are not B-HB responses.** This is the generic case for a law with its own type 𝒳. Then 𝓗 = ∅, so Q3(a) has no witness and Q3(e) gives CARD-STANDARD; c_J(a) ≤ 0 also gives NONJOINT.

4. **Case: Im ⊆ FB.** The defect still bites. About 10³ coordinates identify a B-HB composition with a few dozen parameters, and the single-model rule then fixes its dynamical interface statistics. So no cross pair exists for u₁, u₂ that differ in a declared interface statistic. 𝓗 collapses to the realized diagonal, which lies inside Z(ℛ★), so 𝓗 ∖ Z = ∅. Q5 explicitly allows such witness pairs.

5. **Clauses that might rescue the card do not.**
   - CV-1 resolves ambiguity against the card, so the full-coordinate reading governs.
   - DC-3 decides membership exactly or by certified intervals separated by 2^(−p★). That rules out a "match to resolution" reading, and 10³ coordinates at that resolution are infeasible anyway.
   - BP-7 forbids enlarging FB or dim_lb.
   - §15.4 limits card-added witnesses to HB compositions within the frozen ranges.
   - The DEF-14 sentence mentions "functional in ℛ★" but does not restrict R.
   - c_J(b) and the family cap only lower credit.
   - The outcome contradicts ST-10 / Appendix A, which assume c_J = 1 is reachable. It is a hidden kill of essentially every honest card at S5, which is CR-1 scope under G2-12.

**Verdict:** real, too strict, BLOCKER.

**The proposed fix opens a loophole.** The full-coordinate condition r ∈ cl R is the only thing that currently zeroes c_J(a) when a standard relation links ℛ★'s coordinates to a coordinate that ℛ★ does not read. Two patterns pass after the fix:

- **(i) A pinned response coordinate.** The card pins a non-ℛ★ response coordinate (r' = c), and an 𝒮 relation f = g(u, r') turns this into ℛ★: f = g(u, c).
- **(ii) A response–response relation.** The card realizes a Γ-only relation f = k(r''), and 𝒮 (e.g. STD-13 regression or rate–response) fixes a dynamical interface statistic as u = s(r'').

Today both give 𝓗 ⊆ Z, so c_J(a) = 0. After the fix, r' and r'' are free in the projected hull, so c_J(a) = 1 per instance, up to about 1000 bits. In both cases ℛ★ is really a single-axis (Γ-only) restriction, which Q5 says does not qualify.

No other clause reliably catches these:
- DEF-15 covers only DEF, R1 and mathematical consequences, not 𝒮.
- Q3(a)'s single-axis-consequence exclusion does not fire, because the witness violates the joint (u, f) relation.
- Q3(b) and Q3(c) do not fire, because standard draws have r' ≠ c.
- c_ι is 1 per instance anyway.
- c_J(b) and the family cap do not bind when Im ∩ FB = ∅, and they miss pins that vary per instance.
- NR-17 catches only a pin carried by a cheap, separable sub-conjunct.
- B-SRB catches only when r' is a BP-5 input.

**The correction.** Project the hull as proposed, and carry DEF-15's rule over to 𝒮: a single-axis property that, together with a cited 𝒮 derivation, implies ℛ★ is assessed as that property. This keeps what the full-coordinate condition was doing, and it requires a published 𝒮 derivation. That matches BP-2: the coupling is standard only through 𝒮, not through identifiability of the finite B-HB library. So it does not bring back the kill.

The guard cannot kill an honest card:
- Couplings in Π cannot be reached, because 𝒮 never fixes a hand-supplied Π from Γ.
- Couplings in a dynamical interface statistic are reached only when 𝒮 fixes that statistic from response content, which STD-13 already leaves uncredited.

I also wrote "depends on" rather than "read by", in case ℛ★ is stated through Γ_Π rather than through chart symbols.
verdict.fix_problems:
The proposed fix drops conditioning on the realized values of chart coordinates that ℛ★ does not read. That conditioning is currently the only thing that zeroes c_J(a) for two patterns:

- **(i) Pinned response coordinate.** The law pins a non-ℛ★ response coordinate (r' = c), and an 𝒮 relation f = g(u, r') valid under H turns this into ℛ★: f = g(u, c).
- **(ii) Γ-only relation.** The law realizes a Γ-only relation f = k(r''), and 𝒮 (e.g. STD-13 regression or rate–response) fixes a dynamical interface statistic as u = s(r''), so ℛ★ is f = k(s⁻¹(u)).

Under the current text, 𝓗 ⊆ Z(ℛ★) in both cases, so c_J(a) = 0. Under the fix, r' and r'' are free, so 𝓗 contains points that violate ℛ★, c_J(a) = 1, and b_J can reach about 1000 bits. Yet in both cases ℛ★ is really a single-axis Γ restriction, which Q5 says does not qualify.

Nothing else reliably catches them:
- DEF-15 is limited to DEF-1 to DEF-14, R1's theorems and mathematics.
- Q3(a)'s single-axis-consequence exclusion does not apply, because the witness violates a joint (u, f) relation.
- Q3(b) and Q3(c) pass, because standard draws have r' ≠ c.
- c_ι is 1 per instance in any case.
- c_J(b) and the family cap do not bind when Im ∩ FB = ∅, and they miss pins that vary by instance.
- NR-17 catches only a cheap, separable sub-conjunct.
- B-SRB catches only when r' is a BP-5 input.

**Minor issue.** "Read by ℛ★" is ill-defined if ℛ★ is stated through Γ_Π rather than through chart symbols. "Depends on" is safer.

**Alternative rejected.** Adding auditor-named, 𝒮-linked coordinates to the hull would reintroduce the hidden kill: it empties 𝓗 whenever B-HB cannot reach the card's realized values in an added coordinate. A guard modelled on DEF-15 that requires a cited 𝒮 derivation has no such risk.
verdict.final_wording:
§2.5, Realized coupling, first bullet: replace "U and R are the realized interface and response values over 𝓘, and the **product hull** is 𝓗 := FB ∩ (cl U × cl R), under the single-model rule." with:

"U is the set of realized interface values over 𝓘. R is the set of realized values over 𝓘 of the **ℛ★-coordinates**: the chart coordinates on which ℛ★ or a registered lock observable depends. The **product hull** is 𝓗 := FB ∩ (cl U × cl R), read in the coordinates (u, ℛ★-coordinates). A point is in 𝓗 iff a single m ∈ 𝔐_std(ι | H) realizes it in those coordinates (single-model rule), and m's other chart coordinates are unconstrained. dim_lb and dim_ub are taken in the same coordinates. **Standard consequence of a single-axis property:** if a single-axis property P (Γ-only, or (Π, [h], T)-only) holds on Im, and P together with 𝒮 under H implies ℛ★ by a cited derivation (§13.1, §13.4), then ℛ★ is assessed as P, as in DEF-15 (NONJOINT if P is single-axis; uncredited if P is an open condition)."

§3.1 Q3(a): after "with Obs(m*_F) ∈ 𝓗 ∖ Z(ℛ★)", insert "(read in the coordinates of 𝓗, §2.5)".

Unchanged: Im (the full chart image; non-standard realizations are never removed), FB, c_ι, c_lock, c_J(b), the family cap, the DEF-14 fixed-class rule, and the exclusion of single-axis consequences in Q3(a).

I read the whole charter (frozen_0bc125a.md) and the G2-11 and G2-12 rulings. The E_std part of the defect is real and too strict. The rest is weaker or overstated.

1. E_std is mandatory, and it is charged to Price(𝒦). Q3(c) calls it the card's "frozen, priced" embedding. IP-2 prices "every supplied datum", and E_std is supplied in C12. NR-0 needs it to reproduce the Q3(c) verdict, and CV-1 settles any doubt against the card. The last sentence of Q3(c), "If no E_std is declared … CARD-STANDARD", is unconditional, so every card has to declare one. The B-HB families are continuous or quantum models (harmonic baths, Duffing, HB-10 qubits, NESS baths). They cannot be written natively in a finite L₀ type, so for a realistic card E_std is not the identity. The Appendix-A itemization was carried over from AUDIT_R1_C §2.2, which was written before E_std existed, and its "six components" are X_Π, X_Z, X_h, X_T, Obs and Emb. So the note leaves out E_std. That note is what FREEZE_VERIFICATION §5 item 1 put to the owner, and the owner accepted N_cred = 100 on it in G2-12.

Charging E_std is a design over-charge, not just a missing line in the note:
- E_std produces no credit. b_J, Sol, FB and the lock never read it.
- Its only role is to expose the card to a hostile test (Q3(c)).
- Its cost grows with how far the card's type is from standard models, which cuts against G2-11 item 7 (novelty is judged at the assembled-law level).
- The auditor-substitution clause needs E_std's length only as a bound. It does not need that length added to Price(𝒦).
- At about 100–450 bits, E_std shrinks the c_J = 1 window (price below about 990 bits) from roughly 720–990 to nearly nothing. Honest single-equation cards are therefore pushed to c_J = 2, which needs two independent equations tested at the lock. That is a large hidden tightening.

2. Refutation attempts. These succeed only in part:
- (a) The note is non-normative, but ST-10 in §24.2 is a required-verdict self-test ("SC2 reachable for a compact honest card at c_J = 1"), so the error matters. That verdict still holds at the very low end, so the defect is not a BLOCKER.
- (b) The defect's statement that at c_J = 2 "only the lower half passes" is wrong arithmetic. With b_J = 2000, the bar is about 1990 bits, which covers almost all of its own 890–2090 range.
- (c) Charging ℛ★ under IP-4 is only a hostile-default reading of an ambiguous clause ("relation"). CV-7 lets the owner side with the card on a dispute, so it is not a permanent kill. The proposed IP-4 text also changes nothing: IP-4 charges max(L_stmt, log₂ m), and log₂ m over relations of no greater length is already at most about L_stmt. ℛ★ would still cost about L_stmt(ℛ★).
- (d) s_T is charged legitimately (IP-2, §1.4), and only when T_Π ∉ 𝒯. A compact card can use T_Π ∈ 𝒯, so s_T belongs in the note only as a conditional row. It is not a too-strict rule.
- No other clause rescues the E_std charge. CT-92 and CT-81 deal with dodging embeddings and unexpressive types, not with price.

3. Problems with the proposed fix:
- Replacing "at no greater price" with "meeting these conditions" turns the phrase into "meeting these conditions meeting these conditions". That deletes the only quantitative bound on auditor substitutes. E_std's condition that it "reads no … functional of Γ" has no mechanical enforcement (PC-6's record-factorization test with its c_dec bound covers components, not E_std). An unbounded uniform embedding could therefore compute response-relevant structure from the draw's couplings and steer the card's components into satisfying ℛ★ on at least 1/Q_min of draws. That would be a spurious CARD-STANDARD, so the change creates a new too-strict defect. It is also a tightening, which G2-12 sends to the CR-2 queue rather than CR-1.
- "Any other use → RELOCATED under NR-0" misuses NR-0, which is the undeclared-input rule. A firewall that prices E_std in full when any priced item reuses it is cleaner.
- Removing E_std from Price(𝒦) also lowers the §2.5(b) bar Price(M) ≤ Price(𝒦). That loosens c_J(b) slightly. The loosening is consistent, because E_std is not part of how 𝒦 explains the data, and the family cap (which has no price condition) still applies. Not a loophole.
- With E_std's length kept as the bound on substitutes, a card has no reason to declare an elaborate E_std, because doing so gives auditors a bigger budget. So excluding it from the price opens no card-side loophole.

4. A possible related issue, outside this defect's scope: under IP-6, an E_std that embeds HB-10 quantum draws through the Born rule could count as supplying VB-7, which makes every selectivity result RELOCATED.

Rewriting it as a symmetry clause added only to fix the value is open to the hostile reading "introduced for the purpose".
(3) "Largest window inside which … no verdict changes" sets no minimum width and no resolution floor. If any perturbation breaks Q1 (forced on Sol under exact arithmetic, DC-3), empties Sol (KU-1) or flips NR-5, the window is the single point. Then log₂(R/0) = ∞. The card is NON-COMPRESSIVE at every p, and LOOKUP once ΔL ≤ 0.
(4) The §1.5 robustness neighbourhood covers instance data (𝒞, V, A, τ, 𝒴), not law constants. So it neither rescues the card nor is the intended home for this question.
(5) The §24.1 presumption does not help. RT-19 (REDTEAM_C) prices a short expression at max(L_stmt, tuning price), and here the tuning price is infinite.

(7) Integers in designed roles are protected: truncation levels have DC-4 (n, n+1, 2n) and enumeration bounds have DC-1. Exact rational or integer coefficients in law clauses, and values a symmetry needs, are not protected.

So this is a hidden kill of a legitimate class, not an intended price. It is not a BLOCKER, because cards whose constants all have positive windows are unaffected. That makes it MAJOR. verdict.fix_problems:
The proposed fix opens no material loophole: the max() keeps literal length at p as a floor. It has three wording weaknesses.
(a) "the constant's own" L_stmt is ambiguous for a defined symbol. §4.1 charges only ⌈log₂(#defs+1)⌉ bits per use, so a card could claim a count near 1. The literal-length floor and CV-1 contain this, but the wording should name the whole expression, definitions included.
(b) "literals in R" leaves open which literal types are counted (nat, rat, real at p) and whether token-built expressions count. Each of these is a new ambiguity for CV-1 to settle.
(c) The count needs an enumeration. By Kraft, log₂ of the number of prefix-code expressions no longer than L is at most about L. Charging L_stmt of the stating expression directly is therefore never looser than the count, needs no enumeration, and has no type ambiguity.

A value inside a non-structural window of relative width w needs an expression of about log₂(1/w) bits or more (Elias-δ overhead included). The collapse also needs a second independent literal plus comparison tokens. IP-12 already counts every distinct value tried as a draft. The route only pays for windows narrower than roughly 2^-45 that happen to contain a short rational, which in practice is the honest exact case.
No contradiction found with IP-10, IP-11 (an exact value then needs exact equality with the published value), IP-12, DC-1, DC-4 or CT-41 (still "priced").

One part of the report is overstated. DC-4 levels apply only to FORBID items, so SEL-1 (an ALLOW item) runs at level n only. The conclusion still holds.

T_audit (OR-6, line 1512; App. A line 2660; §18.1(5)). The 60-day clock starts at card freeze, but S9 can only start after S0–S8 are cleared. 1. Expensive runs can shield the card. The fix stops counting the Evaluator's added runs against R_card and gives each run its own R_item. Nothing ties the cost the card declares for those runs to its costs on the counted list. The card could declare cheap costs on the counted list and costs near R_item = 48 core-hours for procedures that only run in charter-side tests. The worst cases are the Q3(c) transplant draws and the NR-7 scrambles, whose number of draws the Evaluator chooses.
